source.title: Neural Expansion: A Unified Mechanism for How Deep Neural Networks Generalize
source.authors: Chashi Mahiul Islam; Samuel Jacob Chacko; Mao Nishino; Can-Lin Zhang; Xiu-Wen Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on ray coverage and measures resulting test accuracy, a conceptual test of a proposed mechanism for generalization. Its measurements do not test the specific behaviors named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The study reports random-label ray coverage, but not whether those models fit random labels or achieve above-chance held-out accuracy. The optimizer comparison reports ray coverage, not a train/test gap. Cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Figure 6 reports the study's own training and test accuracy curves for natural-label and random-label MNIST MLPs, bearing on V1 in a new dataset setting. It also reports MLP and CNN accuracy curves on MNIST and CIFAR-10, bearing on V3. The supplied text preserves axes and legends but not readable curve values, so these results cannot establish a directional verdict. The ray-coverage interventions themselves test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose class-level ray coverage as a geometric mechanism for classification and generalization, and report that coverage interventions change test accuracy. Their population-error argument requires no re-entry; the MNIST restriction result also involves reduced training accuracy, rather than merely a larger generalization gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a ray-coverage intervention, rather than reproducing the original claim's memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or example-removal experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The intervention results differ by dataset and arm; expansion gives a smaller corresponding ray-coverage increase on Fashion-MNIST CNN than on MNIST MLP. Ray coverage is also reported to be nearly seed-invariant and mildly optimizer-sensitive in MNIST MLP/CNN measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Expansion raises test accuracy from 87.38% to 89.04% on MNIST and from 85.27% to 86.37% on Fashion-MNIST; restriction lowers it to 75.18% and 77.86%. GI and coverage move in the corresponding directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary objectives encouraging or discouraging local prediction stability change test accuracy and ray coverage in these two settings.

record.problems: The main intervention uses three random seeds per configuration. The reported intervention outcome is test accuracy, not a measured train/test error gap; for the MNIST-MLP restrict arm, the authors state train accuracy is nearly as low as test accuracy. The causal interpretation is stated under a no-re-entry assumption, and the authors note that without it the conclusion is generally false.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other reported findings such as random-label ray coverage, directional GI evolution, optimizer-related coverage, OOD coverage and adversarial coverage do not measure a behavior named by V1–V8 or a train/test gap; they are summarized in the gate note where relevant.

untested.parts: The original CIFAR-10/ImageNet architectures and recipes are not reproduced. Figure 6's MNIST accuracy outcomes cannot be read from the supplied text.
No width sweep or post-interpolation test-error comparison.
No isolation of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, or initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Optimizer comparisons measure coverage, not held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No dropout or joint dropout/weight-decay removal comparison.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, ranking of generalization gaps, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures. Input Jacobian sensitivity is a different construct.
No removal of examples selected by label memorization and retraining against random-removal controls.

missing.what: Natural-label and random-label MLP training and test accuracy curves are omitted. Recover training fit and held-out accuracy relative to chance for RANDOM-10 and RANDOM-100, together with the natural-label comparator and any recipe differences. Curve values cannot be recovered from this text rendering.

Custom MLP and CNN training/test accuracy curves on the same image datasets are omitted. Recover their test-error comparison and training conditions; the supplied text does not reveal which architecture performs better.

record.verdict_notes: The record's gate overlooks Figure 6, which explicitly reports training and test accuracy, including random-label models. Its rows_left_out statement mentions random-label coverage but does not declare these accuracy results omitted. No directional labels are warranted because their curve values are unreadable in the supplied text. Missing train/test gaps are not a universal reason to exclude results: V1 requires fit and held-out accuracy, and V3 requires comparative test error.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report random-label training fit or held-out accuracy versus chance, or natural-label accuracy for the same recipes.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the interpolation threshold.
No controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparison of test error or local connectivity.
Optimizer comparison reports ray coverage, not held-out performance relative to training performance.
Measures Jacobian singular values and generalization intervals, but does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness against train/test gaps or the stated norm- and margin-based measures.
No example removal or retraining comparison.
